parsed_response.reasoning: The diff shows `minimumTokenResponseSchema` with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` — both produce a literal junk key string (either identical, causing overwrite, or distinct garbage), and neither matches real token-response fields like `expiry_date`/`expires_in`. Zod strips unknown keys by default, so in credential-sharing mode the parsed `.data` retains only `access_token` (plus the manually injected `refresh_token`). Callers then persist this via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })` (e.g. GoogleCalendarService/CalendarService.ts), so the stored credential loses its expiry, and the schema's own comment ('Assume that any property with a number is the expiry') is never satisfied. The defect — expiry silently dropped from refreshed tokens in sync mode — is verifiable directly from the schema code regardless of the exact toString() collision details.

judged_text: Both computed keys in minimumTokenResponseSchema evaluate to the identical string (both derive from z.string().toString()), so the z.number() catchall on line 8 is overwritten by the z.unknown().optional() key on line 9, and zod's default key stripping then removes every field except access_token from the parsed data. In shared-credential mode the 'expiry' property the schema claims to capture (expiry_date, expires_in) is silently dropped from refreshed tokens; callers that persist .data store a credential with no expiry, so expiry-based freshness checks treat the token as always expired and re-hit the sync endpoint on every calendar operation.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined as `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional() })`. Those computed property keys are evaluated immediately as JavaScript strings and will collide (both derive from calling `.toString()` on a Zod schema object), so one overwrites the other in the object literal. Additionally, `z.object(...)` does not implement a wildcard/index-signature this way; unknown keys are stripped by default, so fields like `expiry_date`/`expires_in` will not be retained under this schema. Since `parseRefreshTokenResponse` uses this minimum schema in shared-credential mode, it can indeed drop expiry fields from the parsed data, impacting refresh logic/persistence.
